Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m one of the perinatal mental-health clinicians here. First, congratulations on your new baby; the postpartum weeks can be such a whirlwind of change.

Today I’d like to do a quick check-in using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s a 10-question tool that helps us see how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. It isn’t a test of your parenting—just a way to make sure we’re catching any mood or anxiety symptoms early so we can give you the right support.

Everything you share is confidential, and you can answer honestly without judgment. We’ll go through the questions one by one, and I’ll keep things conversational rather than reading them word-for-word. It usually takes just a few minutes.

Ready to start? 

Over the past week, have you still been able to look forward to things you normally enjoy, or has that sense of enjoyment been hard to come by?

Honestly… most things just feel kind of “meh” right now. I still get little sparks—like when the baby grips my finger or when my husband brought me coffee in bed—but the bigger stuff I used to get excited about, like ordering take-out from our favorite place or binge-watching a show, just feels flat. I’ll go through the motions, but that real lift of “I can’t wait” isn’t there the way it used to be.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I’ve laughed a few times—mostly when my husband made that silly face trying to get the baby to burp—but it feels kind of forced, like I have to remind myself to let go and chuckle. The lighter side doesn’t come as easily or feel as good as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… even simple stuff like the idea of a shower without rushing, or a visit from my best friend, just feels kind of “blah.” I still do them, but that eager, excited feeling I used to get beforehand is pretty much missing.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes—like if the baby won’t settle, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I know logically it’s not always me, but I still catch myself thinking, “A better mom would have figured this out already.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… even when everything’s quiet, I’ll suddenly feel this knot in my chest worrying that the baby’s breathing or that I missed a dirty bottle. Nothing’s actually wrong, but the “what-ifs” still pop up and my heart races.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times—mostly at night—this wave of panic just hits me out of nowhere. My heart starts pounding, I feel shaky, and for a minute I’m sure something awful is about to happen, even though I can’t name what. It passes after a bit, but it’s unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I can juggle the feedings and diapers, but yes—there are stretches where it feels like the pile of tiny clothes, the dishes, and the crying all gang up on me. I’ll suddenly feel like I’m drowning and think, “I can’t keep up,” even though I’m trying my hardest.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

A few nights this week I’ve lain there wired, replaying every little thing I might’ve messed up, and it takes me forever to drift off. Once the baby’s asleep I should be relieved, but instead my mind just keeps buzzing and I can’t settle.
I have felt sad or miserable
Yeah, I’ve had patches of that—like a gray cloud that rolls in for a while, especially in the evenings. It’s not constant, but when it hits I just feel heavy and tear-brimmed for no clear reason.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really full-on crying—just a couple of times I teared up while folding laundry, thinking “I should be happier than this.” It doesn’t turn into sobbing, but the tears sting and I have to blink hard to keep them from falling.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’m tired and overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again and be okay for my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit  
Date: [today’s date]  

Presenting concerns (patient report, 10-item EPDS-styled questionnaire):  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, “gray cloud” most evenings  
- Marked loss of enjoyment/anticipation (“blah” toward shower, visits)  
- Excessive self-blame regarding infant care (“better mom would…”)  
- Recurrent, unprovoked anxiety and nocturnal panic (racing heart, “knot in chest,” dread)  
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning by daily tasks multiple days per week  
- Initial insomnia linked to rumination over perceived mistakes  
- Passive death wish denied; no self-harm ideation endorsed  

Pattern: Symptoms cluster consistent with distress beyond “baby blues,” crossing into possible mild–moderate depressive and anxious states.  

Screening significance:  
- Elevated risk for postpartum depression (low mood, anhedonia, guilt, tearfulness)  
- Elevated risk for postpartum anxiety (unwarranted worry, panic episodes)  
- Protective factors: denies self-harm, engaged partner, reports occasional laughter  

Safety: Negative response to item 10; no further risk indicators elicited today.  

Plan: Review with OB/midwife; consider formal EPDS scoring and referral for perinatal mental-health evaluation if score ≥10 or functional impairment persists.
